messages:
katie: Quick question — hit a confusing behavior in staging. We have a rollout canary that routes 10% to v2, and a feature-flag (beta_flag) that product flips for a cohort. If the flag is true but the rollout guard prevents v2, the feature ends up disabled. Is the intended precedence: rollout routing wins over feature flags (i.e., you can turn the flag on but still be gated by rollout), or should flags be able to opt users into routes?

katie: Example:
```json
// service routing config (console)
{
  "rollouts": [{ "id": "canary-v2", "split": 0.1, "guard": "slo_99_95" }],
  "flags": [{ "name": "beta_flag", "rules": [{ "segment": "beta_users", "value": true }] }]
}
```

tony: Short answer from the runtime side: routing/guard checks happen at the transport/router layer before feature eval. If a guard denies capacity, requests are routed away (or fallback) even if flag says yes. That was deliberate to protect SLOs.

sam: Hmm, product expects feature flags to be the "source of truth" for feature availability. The mismatch is causing surprising behavior for PMs. We need an explicit precedence model in the API/console.

maria: Deploy-note: current order is: 1) routing policy (region/rollout/quotas) 2) guard checks (capacity/SLO) 3) feature flag evaluation 4) model selection. So routing can short-circuit a flag.

katie: That's the root of confusion. Can we make this explicit in the console and expose the resolution trace via telemetry? Proposed minimal changes:
- Add `source`/`origin` tag to flag configs and rollouts (console + API)
- Add an opaque `resolution` field on requests that lists layers checked and final outcome
- Add a console hint on any flag that says "may be subject to routing/guarding" when rollouts are configured

katie: Proposed precedence text to show in UI: "Routing & guard policies may prevent traffic to an enabled flag; use flag + rollout together by creating a rollout that references the flag as a target rule (see pattern below)"

sam: I like the explicit trace. Example pattern (suggested):
```json
{
  "rollouts": [{
    "id": "canary-v2-for-beta",
    "split": 0.1,
    "rules": [{ "if_flag": "beta_flag", "route_to": "v2" }]
  }]
}
```
This makes the intent explicit: flag opt-in triggers the rollout.

tonys: +1 to the trace and to the explicit link. Also: we need a migration/compat plan. Default behavior for existing rollouts should not change. New UI should make the linkage an opt-in.

maria: I'll open two tickets: one for API change (add `resolution` logging + origin metadata) and one for console UX (flag warning + ability to link a rollout to a flag). I'll also add a telemetry event: `feature_resolution` with fields `[request_id, resolved_route, flag_state, guard_state, resolution_path]`.

katie: Can someone capture the API shape we want? Rough sketch:
```json
"resolution": { "layers": ["routing","guard","flag"], "final": "fallback-v1", "trace": ["routing:skipped","guard:denied(slo)","flag:true"] }
```

sam: That should be fine as a start. Also add a short sample log line in structured log: `{"ts":..., "req":..., "flag.beta_flag":true, "rollout": "canary-v2", "resolved_route":"v1", "reason":"guard_denied_slo"}`

deploy-bot: Created ticket PLAT-1429 (API: resolution trace) and PLAT-1430 (Console: flag-rollout UX). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/PLAT-1429

katie: Awesome. Can we also add a small FAQ blurb for PMs: "If your flag appears ignored, check rollouts/guards — routing may be intentionally preventing traffic. To opt flag-driven routing, link the flag to a rollout rule."

tony: I'll prototype the resolution header in the router this sprint and add unit tests for merged semantics. Any objections to the proposed ordering?

sam: No objections. +1 on telemetry and the opt-in linkage pattern.

maria: Ping me when router PR is up; I'll wire telemetry to tracing.

katie: Thanks everyone — saved me from chasing product. We'll update docs once tickets move. :tada:
